strengths: Clear problem formulation with well-articulated motivation for addressing MTP's short-horizon limitations
Novel and scalable approach using single auxiliary head to predict future summaries, effectively addressing the computational scalability of MTP
Comprehensive experimental validation including synthetic tasks (path-star, sibling discovery) that provide excellent intuition for when/why the method works
Large-scale pretraining experiments at both 3B and 8B parameters with diverse benchmarks and multiple random seeds
Strong empirical results at 8B scale on reasoning tasks (ARC-Easy +4.8%, ARC-Challenge +2.8%, MATH +0.9%)
Well-designed synthetic task analysis (Section 3) that elegantly demonstrates the conceptual differences between MTP and FSP variants
Systematic ablations comparing hand-crafted vs learned summaries with clear takeaways about adaptive future representations
weaknesses: Significant scale-dependent effectiveness: DeepSeek-MTP is superior at 3B scale, FSP-RevLM only competitive at 8B scale, with limited analysis of why scaling behavior differs
Computational cost of reverse LM training not adequately addressed; claimed 'amortization' is insufficiently justified, undermining practical applicability especially at smaller scales
Task-dependent and inconsistent improvements: worse than NTP on GSM8K (70.5% vs 71.6%), ties MTP on HumanEval+, with only marginal gains on code generation
Limited theoretical understanding of why learned summaries work; claims about reducing teacher forcing are primarily intuitive rather than formally analyzed
Incomplete analysis: no explanation for why FSP-RevLM scales better than DeepSeek-MTP, limited exploration of future window length sensitivity, no failure case analysis
Methodological concerns: temperature tuned per-method for pass@k (could amplify differences), only 3 random seeds for expensive experiments, MTP constrained to single head for fairness
Reproducibility limitations: custom pretraining dataset not fully detailed, no code release mentioned, reverse LM hyperparameters underspecified, making reproduction difficult
Moderate novelty: combines existing techniques (reverse LM distillation, bag-of-words) without fundamental innovation; incremental advance over prior work

strengths: Clear motivation addressing well-established problems (exposure bias, teacher forcing) in NTP and MTP
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including synthetic analysis, ablations, and large-scale pretraining at 3B and 8B scales
Insightful synthetic task analysis (path-star, sibling discovery) that clearly demonstrates when long-horizon and adaptive summaries provide benefits
Systematic comparison of different future summary strategies (random-skip, multi-hot, learned representations)
Dual approach (hand-crafted and learned summaries) provides useful insights about problem structure
weaknesses: Results are highly inconsistent across model scales: DeepSeek-MTP decisively outperforms FSP-RevLM at 3B scale, improvements only appear at 8B and are task-specific; this undermines generalizability claims
Practical improvements are marginal (typically 1-3% on most tasks; gains of 'up to 5%' are selective). On GSM8K at 8B scale, NTP (71.6%) actually outperforms FSP-RevLM (70.5%)

Questionable experimental setup: (1) iso-data but not iso-compute comparison—training a reverse LM adds real cost dismissed as 'amortized' without justification; (2) artificially restricting MTP to single heads while capable of using more

Weak theoretical justification: the connection between predicting reverse LM representations and exposure bias reduction is informal and never rigorously established. Why should FSP specifically mitigate exposure bias better than MTP?

Poor translation from synthetic tasks to real performance: path-star and sibling discovery experiments show strong benefits (100% vs 47%), but corresponding real-world gains are modest (1-3%), with no clear explanation for the discrepancy
Limited novelty: predicting future summaries is straightforward; using reverse LM as distillation target is incremental. No significant algorithmic or theoretical advance
Weak performance on code generation (MBPP: 1.1% improvement, HumanEval+: tied); gains concentrated narrowly on math/reasoning, questioning robustness
Incomplete analysis: no investigation of what reverse LM representations encode; no sensitivity analysis for τ (Table 3 shows τ=100 sometimes hurts performance); missing ablations on loss weighting
Baseline concerns: DeepSeek-MTP shows anomalously poor performance (ARC-Easy: 0.617 vs NTP 0.718), raising implementation questions; no comparison to other exposure bias methods
Reproducibility limitations: proprietary pretraining data, no code release mentioned, reverse LM training details could be more explicit

strengths: Clear problem motivation with teacher forcing lens applied to reduce teacher forcing degree, providing intuitive framing for the contribution
Excellent synthetic analysis (path-star and sibling discovery tasks) that provides clear conceptual insights into when and why FSP outperforms MTP
Comprehensive large-scale pretraining experiments at both 3B and 8B scales with proper statistical reporting (mean ± s.e. over 3 seeds), which is rare and computationally expensive
Strong empirical results on math reasoning benchmarks (MATH: +4.2%, GSM8K: +3.5%) with consistent improvements across multiple evaluation tasks at 8B scale
Thorough ablation studies (Table 3) systematically analyzing different future-summary strategies and their trade-offs
Demonstrated improved output diversity through learned summaries (Figure 5), addressing an important aspect of generation quality
Well-written paper with clear presentation, good visualizations, and comprehensive reproducibility details in appendices
weaknesses: Computational overhead of reverse language model training not fully accounted for in comparisons; using iso-data rather than iso-compute conditions effectively doubles computational cost but is presented as standard practice without sufficient discussion of practical implications
Mixed results at 3B scale where DeepSeek-MTP outperforms FSP-RevLM on most tasks, limiting practical applicability at smaller model sizes where compute efficiency is critical

Fairness of baseline comparisons: constraining MTP and DS-MTP to single auxiliary heads limits their expressiveness, whereas Table 4 shows multiple MTP heads improve performance on path-star tasks, potentially handicapping baselines
Limited analysis of what the learned reverse-LM representations actually capture; missing ablations isolating the contribution of each component (e.g., MTP + reverse LM distillation separately)
Evaluation benchmarks do not directly probe long-horizon reasoning as motivated; gap between theoretical motivation (long-horizon planning) and empirical evaluation on standard benchmarks
Core novelty is incremental, combining existing techniques (MTP + reverse LM distillation similar to BST/MiM) rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts
Some improvements have overlapping error bars with baselines (e.g., HumanEval+ at 8B: 0.541±0.009), and no statistical significance testing provided to validate claimed improvements
Limited exploration of why DS-MTP outperforms FSP-RevLM at smaller scales, raising questions about when practitioners should use which approach

strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation clearly articulating MTP limitations and proposing an intuitive solution through future summary prediction
Excellent synthetic task analysis (path-star and sibling discovery) that effectively demonstrates when each approach works and provides valuable conceptual insights
Comprehensive large-scale experiments at 3B and 8B scales with diverse benchmarks, thorough ablations, multiple random seeds, and proper error reporting
Consistent empirical improvements on reasoning tasks (e.g., ARC-Easy: +4.8% over NTP, MATH: +0.9% over NTP) with additional benefits in data-constrained regimes
Strong reproducibility practices with detailed architectural specifications, hyperparameters, dataset composition, and extensive supplementary materials
Effective unifying framework that clarifies trade-offs between different future-aware objectives beyond single-method evaluation
weaknesses: Significant computational overhead (2x compute cost from training separate reverse model) not adequately justified relative to modest improvements; missing analysis of alternative compute allocations
Inconsistent improvements across benchmarks: GSM8K shows regression vs NTP (70.5% vs 71.6%), HumanEval+ ties with MTP, suggesting benefits are task-specific rather than general
Scale-dependent performance: DeepSeek-MTP outperforms FSP-RevLM at 3B, only becomes favorable at 8B, raising questions about generality and scalability beyond 8B

Limited practical relevance to modern pretraining: data-constrained regime benefits apply primarily to repeated-epoch training, which is less common as field addresses data wall through larger unique token budgets

Incremental technical novelty: reverse LM approach directly relates to prior work (Twin Networks 2017, MiM 2023, BST 2024); main contribution is demonstrating scale and identifying when learned vs hand-crafted summaries matter
Insufficient analysis of why reverse LM representations work: limited mechanistic understanding of why right-to-left ordering specifically helps or what linguistic properties are captured

Language modeling metrics (NLL/NTA) remain largely unchanged despite larger downstream improvements, raising questions about whether improvements are fundamental vs task-specific or resulting from ensemble effects
Some improvements have overlapping error bars with baselines and lack formal significance testing; 3 random seeds may be insufficient for high-variance tasks like MATH
